title: County of Nevers
capsule: The County of Nevers (Comté de Nevers) was a feudal county in central France along the upper Loire, roughly the later province of Nivernais, with its seat at Nevers. Emerging as a distinct comté in the early eleventh century, it passed by marriage and inheritance through successive houses — counts tied to Burgundy, then to Flanders and the Valois dukes of Burgundy in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries. King Louis XI acquired and exchanged the county in the 1460s, and it remained a comté through the early sixteenth century before Francis I raised it to a duchy in 1539.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's political history is moderately well documented through feudal records; its territorial extent followed the diocese of Nevers and is broadly but not precisely defined.
